A polished homepage means very little if checkout is broken, taxes are wrong, or tracking isn’t firing. Most launch problems aren’t dramatic; they’re small, missed settings that quietly cost sales, but the question is: how are you gonna find those?

This Shopify Store Checklist would help you with that; use it to confirm every part of your store is actually ready, and not just the parts that look finished.

Shopify Store Checklist

Shopify Store Checklist

The first thing we should ensure is the UX, so let’s start with that.

UX

  • Theme is fully mobile-tested, not just desktop-reviewed
  • Navigation, search, and filtering work correctly, including a helpful “no results” page
  • Core Web Vitals are within range: LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1
  • Password page is ready to be removed on launch day, and domain/SSL is connected

Products

  • Every product has accurate descriptions, pricing, and professional photography
  • Unique SKUs assigned to each variant, critical for inventory and analytics as your catalog grows
  • Product weight and dimensions entered accurately; incorrect data leads to wrong shipping charges
  • Collections and categories are organized and easy to browse

Payments

  • Payment gateway fully activated; complete identity verification early since pending checks can disable checkout
  • Multiple payment options enabled (major cards, PayPal, Shop Pay) to avoid losing customers who prefer alternatives
  • At least one test order placed using test mode or a bogus gateway to confirm checkout actually works end to end
  • Payment status correctly syncs from “pending” to “paid” in your order flow

Shipping

  • Shipping zones and rates configured for every region you sell to
  • Carrier-calculated rates tested against real product weights and dimensions
  • Tax settings configured correctly for your regions; this is both a compliance and trust issue
  • At least one full test order used to confirm shipping and tax calculate correctly at checkout

SEO

  • Metadata (titles, descriptions) set for key pages and products
  • Structured data implemented for products and organization info
  • Internal linking in place between related products, collections, and content
  • Site speed and Core Web Vitals reviewed, since both affect search visibility, not just UX

Analytics

  • Google Analytics 4 installed and verified as firing correctly
  • Ad pixels (Meta, Google Ads, etc.) installed and tested before any paid traffic runs
  • Event tracking confirmed for key actions: product views, add-to-cart, and purchases, with correct product and variant IDs

Security

  • SSL active and domain properly connected
  • Staff account permissions reviewed, especially if multiple people manage the store
  • Apps audited, unused or redundant apps removed to reduce both risk and performance drag

Conversion Tracking

  • Full purchase funnel tested from homepage to order confirmation, not just the homepage
  • Abandoned cart tracking and recovery emails configured
  • Transactional emails (order confirmation, shipping updates) tested and confirmed to send correctly
  • Legal pages published: privacy policy, terms, and return policy, both a trust and compliance requirement

Before You Remove the Password Page

Run through this checklist one more time end to end. A store can look complete and still fail at the basics: checkout untested, taxes misconfigured, or tracking not firing. If any section above isn’t fully checked, resolve it before launch day, not after.
